hints.title: Ordered Array Extraction
hints.text: An in-order traversal of the tree visits nodes in strictly non-decreasing sorted order.

hints.title: Bisection Lookup
hints.text: Flatten tree values into a sorted list. For each query, perform binary search to locate the insertion index.

hints.title: Boundary Value Resolution
hints.text: The greatest value less than or equal to q is the element immediately before or at the insertion index. The smallest value greater than or equal to q is the element at the lower bound.

hints.title: In-Order Flattening and Bisection Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def closestNodes(self, root, queries: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
        vals = []
        def inorder(node):
            if not node:
                return
            inorder(node.left)
            vals.append(node.val)
            inorder(node.right)
        inorder(root)
        n = len(vals)
        ans = []
        for q in queries:
            idx = bisect.bisect_right(vals, q)
            mini = vals[idx - 1] if idx > 0 else -1
            if idx > 0 and vals[idx - 1] == q:
                maxi = q
            else:
                maxi = vals[idx] if idx < n else -1
            ans.append([mini, maxi])
        return ans
```

variables: n: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Linear tree in-order traversal followed by logarithmic binary search for each query.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing an unbalanced tree directly per query incurs worst-case O(q * n) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary list storing in-order sorted values.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Flattens tree to guard against degenerate BST depth and guarantees O(log n) query bounds.
